..
The broad trough extending from tropical disturbance 98W in eastern
Yap State has finally made it to the region, to then exit to the west
as another convergence zone forms in its place, bringing patchy 
showers and some thunderstorms Saturday and Saturday night. 
Diffusive flow will ensue thereafter, allowing mostly pleasant 
weather to return to the Marianas beginning early next week.

Marine...
Combined seas of 6 to 8 feet will persist through Saturday and then 
begin to slowly taper down thereafter, as northeasterly swell and 
westerly swells continue to diminish. A moderate risk of rip 
currents is expected along north, east, and west facing reefs of the 
Marianas through Saturday night. Then, rip current risk may drop to 
low along west facing reefs as the aforementioned swells decrease.

Tropical Systems...
A developing tropical disturbance, the Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
(JTWC)'s Invest 97W, is centered over the northern Marshall Islands 
near 11N166E, and has moved very little over the last 24 hours. As of
1130 AM ChST (0130 UTC), Invest 97W is now the subject of a Tropical
Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA), rated "high" for development, 
meaning development into a significant tropical cyclone (a Tropical 
Depression) is expected within 24 hours. Himawari visible satellite 
imagery this afternoon shows widespread showers and isolated 
thunderstorms across the Marshalls north of Majuro, extending 
eastward to beyond the Date Line, within a broad, elongated region of
cyclonic turning. Deep convection is building over and just west of 
the center in the vicinity of Enewetak, Bikini, and Rongelap Atolls. 
Models favor 97W developing rapidly in the next few days, remaining 
quasi-stationary through Saturday before gradually lifting north out 
of the RMI around Saturday night, likely as a tropical depression or 
even a low-end tropical storm. The track of 97W then becomes more 
uncertain, with most solutions showing a very slow northeast 
meandering through early next week, before an eventual westward turn 
by the end of next week. 

In the meantime, Invest 97W will maintain a wet and gusty pattern
across the northern Marshalls for the next day or two. 
Scatterometry from this morning showed fresh to strong westerly 
winds just south of 97W's center, over the westernmost islands and 
atolls of the central RMI. Surface observations on Kwajalein Island 
show moderate to fresh westerly winds with frequent strong gusts 
over 25 mph, and significant boat damage was reported this morning
there along western exposures. Westerly winds over the central 
western Marshalls will strengthen and shift southwesterly through the
weekend as 97W develops and moves northward. This will be closely 
monitored for additional impacts across the Marshall Islands, and a 
Special Weather Statement was issued for Majuro and the 
central/northern RMI.

Another weak tropical disturbance is seen over far eastern Yap
State near 9N147E, JTWC's Invest 98W. 98W is a very broad, weak 
circulation spanning nearly the entirety of Yap and Chuuk States. 
Most of the convection is seen within the south to south-southwest 
flow along its eastern periphery, covering Chuuk Lagoon and Satawal,
and to the west near Yap. Along the northern edge of Invest 98W, 
scattered showers are seen within a westward-propagating trade-wind 
trough, moving across the northern CNMI this afternoon. Invest 98W 
is still rated "sub-low," meaning it is not favored to develop much 
in the next few days as it continues westward across Yap State. 
However, it still looks to maintain generally wetter conditions for 
Chuuk tonight, and the Marianas through the weekend.

For more information on Invest 97W, see bulletins issued by JTWC 
under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW. Additional information on Invest 
98W may be found there as well, if it becomes rated "low" for 
development or higher.

Eastern Micronesia...
Pohnpei and Kosrae remain within a fairly dry ridging pattern this
afternoon, while Majuro sits just southeast of developing Invest 97W,
discussed in the Tropical Systems section above. Numerous to
widespread showers are seen across the Marshall Islands north of
Majuro Atoll, but are scattered near Majuro itself. Invest 97W,
currently centered near 11N166E, will be the primary weather concern
within eastern Micronesia for the next few days, producing a surge in
west winds and swell across the central and northern RMI as it
strengthens near Rongelap Atoll. A Special Weather Statement was
issued earlier this afternoon for impacts related to Invest 97W.
Moderate west to southwest winds with strong gusts to 25 kts are 
expected for Majuro through Sunday as 97W gradually lifts north out
of the Marshall Islands, but most of the showers are expected to stay
north of Majuro. Locally heavy showers will be possible tonight, and
outflow boundaries could produce strong gusts at times, with higher
winds, gusts, and impacts expected for islands and atolls along the
